page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is a cost-optimized cloud virtual machine utilizing the ARM64 architecture under the QEMU hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, offering 4 shared vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with one thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in approximately 1.95 GB per core and a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Local persistent storage includes an integrated 80 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark results demonstrate average synthetic processor throughput under stress-ng, scoring 1777.99 in single-core and 7055.54 in multi-core metrics. Memory subsystems show stable throughput for large-block operations, registering uncached read speeds of 45.11 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 26.08 GB/sec. PassMark database operations also place in the median bracket at 2684.51 points. However, broader compute benchmarks reflect modest single-threaded efficiency, with Geekbench recording 1005.0 single-core and 3335.0 multi-core scores, alongside reduced rates in compression, static web delivery (4.52 GB/sec), and LLM text generation.

Positioned within Hetzner's ARM-based budget tier, the cax21 delivers high core density and predictable concurrent execution for its resource profile. The primary architectural tradeoff stems from shared core allocation and lower single-thread throughput relative to high-frequency x86 offerings, accompanied by the absence of AVX instruction sets. Consequently, the instance is well suited for multi-threaded lightweight web services, containerized microservices, development and testing environments, and localized relational or key-value caching workloads that do not demand extensive memory allocations or dedicated bare-metal CPU pinning.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an ARM64-based virtual server belonging to the provider's cost-optimized tier, virtualized via QEMU. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.0 GHz across 4 physical cores, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The platform does not bundle discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addressing. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves median results in stress-ng compute tests and large-block memory transfers, alongside mid-range PassMark database performance. Conversely, single-core processing in Geekbench and tasks such as compression and LLM inference fall into lower tiers. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and shared CPU resources, the cax21 is tailored for cost-effective microservices, background task processing, testing and staging deployments, and lightweight distributed caching layers that benefit from multi-core ARM architectures without requiring dedicated core isolation.
